verses.text: Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South, and lived between Kadesh and Shur. He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.
Abraham said about Sarah his wife, “She is my sister.” Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Behold, you are a dead man, because of the woman whom you have taken. For she is a man’s wife.”
Now Abimelech had not come near her. He said, “Lord, will you kill even a righteous nation?
Didn’t he tell me, ‘She is my sister?’ She, even she herself, said, ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands I have done this.”
God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also withheld you from sinning against me. Therefore I didn’t allow you to touch her.
Now therefore, restore the man’s wife. For he is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. If you don’t restore her, know for sure that you will die, you, and all who are yours.”
Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ear. The men were very scared.

Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done!”
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What did you see, that you have done this thing?”
Abraham said, “Because I thought, ‘Surely the fear of God is not in this place. They will kill me for my wife’s sake.’
Besides, she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.
When God caused me to wander from my father’s house, I said to her, ‘This is your kindness which you shall show to me. Everywhere that we go, say of me, “He is my brother.”’”
Abimelech took sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and restored Sarah, his wife, to him.
Abimelech said, “Behold, my land is before you. Dwell where it pleases you.”
To Sarah he said, “Behold, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. Behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes to all that are with you. In front of all you are vindicated.”
Abraham prayed to God. God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his female servants, and they bore children.
For Yahweh had closed up tight all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

footnotes.content: I see Abraham once more moving toward the South, settling between Kadesh and Shur as a foreigner in Gerar. Even the one called by God still lives far from the land of promise for now. Yet the Lord who called him remains near him still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: It grieves me to see Abraham fall into the same fear he did in Egypt, saying Sarah is his sister. Fear makes us forget that the God who protected us before is still able to protect us now. How quick we are to lean on our own devices when we ought to lean on Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Behold, the Lord meets Abimelech in the night with a word that wakes him to the truth: Sarah belongs to Abraham. I am thankful that God speaks even to those outside the covenant to guard what He has promised. Our God is a faithful keeper of those He has called.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech pleads with the Lord, calling Him 'Lord' and appealing to righteousness. It does my old heart good to see a man who sought to do right appeal to the God who knows the heart. The Lord is never deaf to those who turn to Him in reverent fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech speaks honestly before God, telling Him of the integrity of his heart and the innocence of his hands. I take comfort that our God is not fooled, yet He also discerns the difference between deceit and ignorance. He judges righteously, and He is also merciful to those who walk in what light they have.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How tender is this word: the Lord Himself says He withheld Abimelech from sinning against Him. I have learned in my years that our greatest restraint is often the grace of God keeping our hand back. Even before we knew to pray, He was mercifully holding us from what would have grieved us both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord calls Abraham a prophet here, the first time we see that title in Scripture. It is a reminder that God uses flawed men to speak for Him and to pray for others. I find great comfort that Abraham must pray for Abimelech, for it shows the God of mercy calls His people to intercede even after their failure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech rises early and tells all his servants, and they are very afraid. When God speaks plainly, fear of Him falls rightly upon those who hear. May the Lord grant us such a holy fear, not the fear of man, but the fear that leads us to repent and to make things right.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech rightly confronts Abraham, asking why he has brought such a great sin upon him and his kingdom. I have learned that our little fears, when acted upon, can bring trouble far beyond ourselves. May the Lord give us courage to trust Him, so that we need not wound others by our unbelief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech asks Abraham what he saw that made him do this thing. It is a piercing question for any believer. How often do we look at our circumstances and forget the God who has already done so much for us? May we learn to look to Him first, and not to the fears our eyes see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham confesses the root of it all: he thought there was no fear of God in that place. I know that thought well, for unbelief always begins by forgetting who God is and where He is. But the Lord proved Abraham wrong here, for He was there to guard Sarah and to restrain Abimelech by His fear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham admits the half-truth: Sarah is indeed his sister by his father, though not by his mother, and she became his wife. I see here a man trying to justify a sin by mixing truth with deceit. Our God calls us not to clever words, but to simple trust and faithful honesty before Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham tells how this became a habit, a plan made when God caused him to wander from his father's house. Habits of fear, once formed, are hard to break, but our God is faithful to break them by grace. I am thankful that the Lord does not cast off His people for their repeated failures, but restores and teaches them still.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech acts with generosity, giving sheep, cattle, servants, and restoring Sarah to Abraham. I see a beautiful thing here: the man whom Abraham wronged is the one showing kindness to him. Our God often uses the kindness of strangers to restore what our own fear has put at risk.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech gives Abraham free leave to dwell wherever it pleases him in his land. What mercy, that the one who could have dealt harshly instead opens his land to the man who had deceived him. I am reminded that the God of all grace can turn reproach into unexpected kindness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abimelech gives Sarah a thousand pieces of silver as a covering of the eyes, vindicating her before all. I take note that God cares deeply for the reputation of His people, even when they have been caught in weakness. Our Lord is not only our shield, but He also restores our honor by His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abraham prays, and God heals Abimelech and his household. I find this touching: the man who failed to pray for Sarah's protection must now pray for those he had wronged. Our God delights to answer the prayers of His people, using them to bring healing even after their own stumbling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord had closed every womb in Abimelech's house because of Sarah, Abraham's wife. Yet now, through Abraham's prayer, He opens them again. I see here the faithfulness of God to guard the promise of the child He has spoken, and His mercy to restore those who feared Him. He is both just and the justifier.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
